Save one frame of an animation as a still image

Source: R/animate.R
anim_frame.Rd

anim_frame() writes a single frame of a vellum_animation to a PNG, SVG or PDF file: the poster for an animation, its thumbnail, or the moment to put in print. The frame is drawn exactly as it appears in the animation – the same frozen scales and colours, the same tween, the same frame variables in the title – so a poster matches the animation it stands for, which a separately built static plot (its scales trained on one state) need not.

Usage

anim_frame(filename, animation, frame = NULL, scale = 1)

Arguments

filename

Output path; .png, .svg or .pdf.

animation

A vellum_animation (from animate()).

frame

The frame to save: a whole number from 1 to the number of frames. The default is the frame a reader who asks for reduced motion sees: the last frame when the animation ends on its final state (a reveal, transition_time(), a non-looping transition_states()), else the first.

scale

Resolution multiplier (default 1), as in render_plot(): 2 doubles the pixels of a PNG at the same layout.

Value

filename, invisibly.

Details

Frames are numbered as in the files anim_save() writes, pauses and rewind included (see animate()).

See also

anim_save(), animate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
d <- data.frame(t = rep(1:3, each = 4), g = rep(letters[1:4], 3),
                v = c(1, 3, 2, 4, 4, 1, 3, 2, 2, 4, 1, 3))
a <- vplot(d) |>
  mark_bar(x = g, y = v, fill = g) |>
  transition_states(t, wrap = FALSE) |>
  animate()
anim_frame("poster.png", a) # the final state
anim_frame("middle.svg", a, frame = 25)
} # }
